title: A Protocol for a Novel Human Ex Vivo Model of Aneurysm
protocol: Obtain human umbilical cords, covered under existing ethical approval.
Store umbilical cords in serum-free media at 4°C immediately after being obtained.
Dissect umbilical cord samples, limiting the time between harvest and usage within the bioreactor setup to 90 ± 30 min.
Under sterile conditions, place a length of umbilical cord within a sylgard petri dish.
Identify the two arteries and one vein by observing a cross-section of the umbilical cord.
Partially open the cord and pin down on the dish.
Micro-dissect the arteries under PBS containing penicillin and streptomycin at 4°C, flushing with PBS to remove blood clots.
Transfer dissected arteries into serum-free DMEM at 4°C for immediate use.
Sterilize tissue culture hoods with Milton sterilizing solution.
Place bioreactor chambers in Milton sterilizing solution for at least 2 hours, then wash briefly in sterile water and place under a tissue culture hood to dry.
Cut arteries stored in serum-free DMEM at 4°C into three equal lengths of 5 cm for baseline, untreated, and treated conditions.
Connect short silicon tubes at both ends of the bioreactor chamber.
Mount arteries between two small cannulae using sutures to tie each artery onto a cannula.
Connect each cannula to the short silicon tube and place inside a supporting bioreactor chamber.
Fill long silicon tube with 10% FBS/DMEM and pass through a peristaltic pump to close the system, permitting laminar flow induction within an incubator.
Subject each chamber to pulsatile flow conditions with a flow rate of 6.5 dyn/cm² at 37°C and 5% CO₂ for 72 hours.
Use untreated chambers with 80 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM as controls.
For Ang II-treated arteries, supplement 80 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM with 5 μM Angiotensin II.
For intervention-treated chambers, add the corresponding intervention to 80 mL of 10% FBS/DMEM.
After 72 hours of flow within the bioreactor chambers, remove the arteries carefully.
Dispose of the two edges of the artery not subjected to laminar flow where they were sutured to the cannula.
Cut the remaining artery into proximal and distal segments.
Fix the proximal segment in 10% formalin for histology.
Store the distal segment in a −80°C freezer for downstream genomic/proteomic analysis.
Cut the proximal portion of the artery (approx. 2.5 cm in length) into five 5 mm rings for subsequent histological processing and wax embedding.
From the formalin-fixed, wax-embedded arterial rings, cut 3 μm sections onto adhesive glass microscope slides (two sections per slide).
Cut 3 μm sections from formalin-fixed wax-embedded arterial rings.
Place two sections per slide on adhesive glass microscope slides.
Perform Elastin van Gieson (EVG) histochemical staining using an automated stainer or manual protocol.
Coverslip sections using a relevant mounting medium such as DPX.
Visualize the sections using a bright field microscope at ×20 magnification.
Acquire images under ×20 magnification.
Determine the relative amount of elastin using a computerized image analysis program and express as an average percentage of the arterial cross-sectional area.
Perform haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histochemical staining using an automated stainer or manual protocol.
After H&E staining, coverslip sections using a relevant mounting medium such as DPX.
Visualize the sections using a bright field microscope.
Acquire images under ×20 magnification.
Count the number of nuclei and express as an average percentage of the arterial cross-sectional area.
Cut 3 μm sections from formalin-fixed wax-embedded arterial rings, placing two sections per slide on adhesive glass microscope slides.
Perform picrosirius red histochemical staining (0.1% (w/v) Sirius Red F3B saturated aqueous picric acid, pH 1.8–2.2).
After picrosirius red staining, coverslip sections using a relevant mounting medium such as DPX.
Visualize the sections using a bright field polarizing microscope.
Acquire images under ×20 magnification.
Cut 3 μm sections from formalin-fixed wax-embedded arterial rings onto adhesive glass microscope slides (two sections per slide).
Dewax sections by placing in three changes of Clearene for 5 min each.
Rehydrate sections by placing in three changes of graduated alcohol (100%, 90%, and 70%) for 5 min each.
Rinse sections in distilled H2O.
Place slides in a black trough with 10 mM citrate acid pH 6.0.
Heat slides for 6 min full power in microwave.
Top up with distilled water and heat again for 6 min full power in microwave.
Allow to cool for 30 min.
Rinse slides in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 3 × 2 min.
Dry back of slide with tissue paper.
Encircle sections with wax pen.
Place within a humidified chamber.
Inhibit endogenous peroxidase activity with Bloxall endogenous blocking solution for 10 min at 18°C–22°C.
Rinse slides in PBS for 3 × 2 min.
Pipette on 50 μL of 10% horse serum.
Incubate at 18°C–22°C for 30 min.
Tap off solution and dry back of slides.
Pipette on 50 μL of either mouse anti-human alpha-smooth muscle actin (1/200) or rat anti-human ER-TR7 (1/250), diluted in PBS.
Incubate for 16–18 h at 4°C.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 2 min.
Dry back of slides with tissue and pipette on 50 μL of horse anti-mouse biotinylated ready-to-use antibody or goat anti-rat biotinylated ready-to-use antibody, diluted 1/200 in PBS.
Incubate at 18°C–22°C for 30 min.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 2 min.
Dry back of slides with tissue and pipette on 50 μL DyLight-488-conjugated Streptavidin (10 μg/mL).
Incubate at 18°C–22°C for 1 h.
Wash sections in PBS for 3 × 2 min.
Mount slides with appropriately sized coverslip and Vectashield antifade mounting medium with DAPI.
